subject.title: [Feature Request] Add config encryption for credentials at rest

question: Which credential-at-rest model should OpenClaw adopt for stored gateway, channel, and provider secrets?
rationale: The code path is clear, but the permanent model changes key custody, unattended startup, migration, recovery, and auth-provider compatibility, so automation should not choose it without maintainer/security intent.

options.title: Design native credential-at-rest encryption
options.body: Define a supported keychain or passphrase-backed storage model with doctor migration, recovery behavior, rotation guidance, and tests for config plus SQLite auth profiles.

options.title: Keep SecretRefs as the supported mitigation
options.body: Narrow this issue to docs and audit guidance and explicitly decide that transparent encryption is out of scope for now.

options.title: Land partial auth-store sealing first
options.body: Use the open auth-store sealing work as a stepping stone while keeping this issue open for openclaw.json, backups, and migration coverage.

recommendation.title: Design native credential-at-rest encryption
recommendation.body: Define a supported keychain or passphrase-backed storage model with doctor migration, recovery behavior, rotation guidance, and tests for config plus SQLite auth profiles.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved design must cover the SQLite auth-profile persistence refactor and broader config/auth compatibility boundary that steipete recently authored or touched.
